      # apt has no jj package, hence the release tarball. Pinned to the jj-lib version in
      # vcs/Cargo.toml: bump both together.
      - name: Install protoc + jj
        env:
          JJ_VERSION: 0.43.0
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq protobuf-compiler
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \
            | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ./jj
          jj --version

      # Pinned for the lint gates below, unlike the `app` job (which deliberately tracks the runner's
      # rustc so a toolchain bump invalidates its output cache). rustfmt's layout and clippy's lint set
      # both change between releases, so an unpinned toolchain makes `--check` and `-D warnings` fail
      # when GitHub rolls its image rather than when someone's code is wrong. Same reasoning as the
      # pinned golangci-lint in `cli`. Keep in step with the local toolchain.
      - name: Install Rust 1.96.1
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install 1.96.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
          rustup default 1.96.1

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: vcs

      # Ordered cheapest-first so a formatting nit doesn't wait on the jj-lib crate graph.
      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml

  app:
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Xcode 16+ bundles swift-format (used by `make app-lint`) and builds for macOS 14+.
      - uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1
        with:
          xcode-version: latest-stable

      # Scripts/build-helper.sh compiles + embeds the workroom CLI during the test build.
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      # jj (Jujutsu) is required by WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests, which exercise the VCS
      # status resolver against real git + jj repos. git + gh are preinstalled on the runner;
      # jj is not. XcodeGen generates the (gitignored) .xcodeproj. protobuf provides protoc, a
      # build-time dependency of jj-lib (the Rust VCS core, built by `make app-vcs`).
      # aws/tap ships pre-tapped but untrusted on the runner image, which makes every `brew
      # install` on this job emit a "tap trust" warning annotation unrelated to our formulae.
      - name: Install XcodeGen + jj + protobuf
        run: |
          brew untap aws/tap
          brew install xcodegen jj protobuf

      - name: Lint (swift-format --strict)
        run: make app-lint

      # The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links. `make app-vcs` runs
      # vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh to produce the WrVcs package's xcframework + Swift bindings, and
      # MUST run before SPM resolves that local package below. Rust is preinstalled on the runner.
      #
      # Cache the *outputs*, not cargo's state: they only change when vcs/ (or the compiler) does,
      # which most commits don't touch, so the whole ~4min crate-graph build is skipped outright.
      # The key mirrors the input hash build-apple.sh stamps, so a restored set is also a no-op for
      # the app-vcs dep of `make app-test` below. rustc's version is in the key because it's in that
      # hash — leaving it out would mean a toolchain bump hits the cache, rebuilds anyway, and (the
      # primary key having hit) never saves the result.
      - name: Rust toolchain version (cache key input)
        id: rust
        run: |
          # e.g. "rustc 1.96.1 (31fca3adb 2026-06-26)" → "1.96.1-31fca3adb" (cache-key-safe).
          echo "version=$(rustc --version | awk '{print $2 "-" $3}' | tr -d '()')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Cache VCS core outputs
        id: vcs-core
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks
            vcs/swift/WrVcs/Sources/WrVcs/wr_vcs_uniffi.swift
            vcs/swift/WrVcs/Sources/wr_vcs_uniffiFFI/include
          key: >-
            wrvcs-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}-${{
            hashFiles('vcs/**/*.rs', 'vcs/**/Cargo.toml', 'vcs/Cargo.lock', 'vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh') }}

      # Cold path only (vcs/ changed): keep cargo itself incremental. Swatinem/rust-cache rather than
      # a hand-rolled actions/cache of ~/.cargo + vcs/target, which restored a target/ whose
      # fingerprints were always stale — every run recompiled all 257 crates on a cache *hit*, and
      # the hit meant the useless cache was never re-saved.
      - name: Cache cargo (cold path)
        if: steps.vcs-core.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: vcs

      - name: Build VCS core (Rust → xcframework + Swift bindings)
        if: steps.vcs-core.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: make app-vcs

      # SPM resolves ~15 packages (Sparkle, Sentry, libghostty, the tree-sitter grammars, and
      # swift-syntax pulled transitively) by cloning them from GitHub on every run. Cache the
      # resolved checkouts keyed on project.yml (the sole source of the dependency set — the
      # .xcodeproj is xcodegen-generated and gitignored) so an unchanged set skips the network
      # entirely. The restore-keys fallback reuses an older cache after a dep change so only the
      # delta is fetched.
      - name: Cache SPM packages
        id: spm
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages
          key: spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('macapp/project.yml') }}
          restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Compiling the dependency graph — libgit2 (429 tasks), SwiftGitX, the tree-sitter grammars,
      # Sentry, Sparkle, swift-syntax — is ~60% of the build's work and none of it changes between
      # runs. Caching the build dir lets xcodebuild's incremental check reuse those objects; only our
      # own sources rebuild (checkout gives them fresh mtimes, while the restored dep checkouts keep
      # their original ones, so the dependency objects stay up to date).
      #
      # Deliberately NO run-id suffix or restore-keys: the key is exactly what the dep objects depend
      # on (compiler + the dependency set), so the first run saves and every later run hits without
      # paying to re-upload ~500MB each time. actions/cache is post-if success(), so a failed build's
      # dir is never saved.
      - name: Xcode version (cache key input)
        id: xcode
        run: |
          # e.g. "Xcode 26.0" + "Build version 17A324" → "26.0-17A324".
          echo "version=$(xcodebuild -version | awk 'NR==1{v=$2} NR==2{b=$NF} END{print v "-" b}')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Cache Xcode build dir
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: macapp/DerivedData/Build
          key: >-
            xcbuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.xcode.outputs.version }}-${{
            hashFiles('macapp/project.yml') }}

      # Resolve up front with retries so a transient github.com blip mid-clone can't fail the whole
      # run (it did: swift-syntax clone hit "Couldn't connect to server"). The subsequent app-test
      # build reuses these checkouts via the same -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath, so it won't re-clone.
      #
      # Skipped on an exact cache hit: there's nothing to clone, so the whole step (~25s, including an
      # xcodegen run that `make app-test` does again anyway) is pure overhead. A restore-keys-only
      # (partial) restore reports no cache-hit, so a dependency change still resolves here, retries
      # and all.
      - name: Resolve SPM packages (retry on network flake)
        if: steps.spm.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        working-directory: macapp
        run: |
          xcodegen generate
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj -scheme WorkroomApp \
              -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages \
              -resolvePackageDependencies && exit 0
            echo "::warning::SPM resolve attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 15s"
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "::error::SPM resolve failed after 3 attempts"; exit 1

      # Hosted runners have no signing cert / dev team: ad-hoc sign, clear the team, manual
      # style so xcodebuild won't provision against Apple's servers. Lets the non-sandboxed
      # app build and the unit tests launch their host app. (`make app-test` also builds.)
      - name: Test
        run: >-
          make app-test
          APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="

      # The supervisor PTY integration test (issue #7) drives the real supervisor.sh under a pty with
      # a fake server — the only gate on the no-orphan / no-"already running" behaviour the Swift unit
      # tests (mocked seam) can't see. python3 is preinstalled on the macOS runner.
      - name: Test (run-command supervisor)
        run: make app-test-supervisor

      # Shell-script tests. `make app-test` builds Debug with a single native arch, so it can never
      # exercise build-helper.sh's multi-arch path — the branch whose absence shipped an arm64-only
      # CLI inside every universal .app. These run it directly with ARCHS="arm64 x86_64".
      - name: Test (build + channel helper scripts)
        run: make app-test-scripts

                -o "$out/$bin" .

          gh release view nightly >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
            gh release create nightly --prerelease --title "nightly" \

  # the nightly appcast item, then stamp the release title with the version as the skip marker.

          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security import "$CERT" -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$KEYCHAIN"

      # tripwires and the universal-arch cases. Runs BEFORE the release step, or it is not a gate.
      #
      # `make app-release` cannot depend on this itself: app-test builds Debug, which pins automatic
      # "Apple Development" signing (project.yml), and this runner imports only a Developer ID cert.
      # Hence the same ad-hoc overrides ci.yml uses.
      - name: Test (artifact gate)
        run: >-
          make app-test
          APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="

      - name: Build, sign, notarize, staple, package DMG
        env:
          NOTARY_KEY: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY }}
          NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
          SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Sentry dSYM upload (optional — release.sh skips when any is empty). Without these the
          # nightly shipped unsymbolicated every night, which is why the app frames in WORKROOM-2B's
          # hang report were three unnamed addresses. ORG/PROJECT are slugs, not secrets, but kept as
          # secrets to match this job's convention (and release.yml's).
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          # release.sh derives MARKETING_VERSION = ${VERSION#v} and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = commit
          # count; the nightly version has no leading v, so it flows through unchanged.
        run: |
          echo "$NOTARY_KEY" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8"
          # CONFIGURATION=Nightly builds the side-by-side "Workroom Nightly" identity (bundle id,
          # name, icon, pinned nightly channel) instead of the main "Workroom" app.
          CONFIGURATION=Nightly NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-release

      - name: Upload nightly DMG
        run: |
          # Fixed, version-independent name so the appcast enclosure URL is stable across nights.
          ASSET="$RUNNER_TEMP/workroom-macos-app_nightly.dmg"
          cp "macapp/build/release/Workroom Nightly.dmg" "$ASSET"
          gh release upload nightly "$ASSET" --clobber

      - name: Publish Sparkle appcast (nightly channel)
        env:
          TAG: nightly
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: macapp/Scripts/appcast.sh

      - name: Stamp nightly release with the version (skip marker)
        # LAST step: written only after assets + appcast succeed, so a partial run retries.
        run: gh release edit nightly --title "${VERSION}"

    needs: release
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1

          xcode-version: latest-stable

      # Scripts/build-helper.sh compiles + embeds the workroom CLI into the app bundle.

      # current, satisfying jj-lib's 1.93 MSRV).

      - name: Import Developer ID signing certificate

          MACOS_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          CERT="$RUNNER_TEMP/dev-id.p12"
          KEYCHAIN="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$CERT"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security import "$CERT" -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PWD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN" login.keychain

      - name: Build, sign, notarize, staple, package DMG
        env:
          NOTARY_KEY: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY }}
          NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
          # Sparkle: injects the tag as the app version and EdDSA-signs the DMG for the appcast.
          # Empty until the secret is added — release.sh then skips signing (DMG still ships).
          SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          # Sentry dSYM upload (optional — release.sh skips when any is empty). ORG/PROJECT are
          # slugs, not secrets, but kept as secrets here to match this job's convention.
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          echo "$NOTARY_KEY" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8"
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="
          NOTARY_KEY_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/notary.p8" make app-release

      - name: Upload installer to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |

          cp macapp/build/release/Workroom.dmg "$ASSET"
          gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$ASSET" --clobber

      - name: Publish Sparkle appcast
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: macapp/Scripts/appcast.sh
